To support students in achieving their next steps, IAG – information, advice and guidance – play a critical role in our admissions process to the sixth form. It is essential that students are placed on the right courses that ensure their future success. We offer students a broad curriculum at different levels from A-levels, BTECs and T-levels. Most are delivered on-site but some are delivered in-conjunction with partnerships with Park High School and Barnet Football Club.
We challenge our students to be the best versions of themselves they can be as well as providing a range of pastoral support to help them overcome obstacles to learning. We ask all our students to make a contribution to the school, local or international community and as a result they are looked on as role models by younger students.
Success as a student will be influenced by your contribution to, and participation in the working of this community as well as your motivation and the development of good professional working habits. Students take pride in participating in community, careers and challenge enrichment. We believe that innovation and technological solutions allows us to both reach further, longer and in more individual ways and to stretch our community almost endlessly beyond the physical space and timetabled hours to get to that excellence.
We look forward to welcoming you to Canons Sixth Form and watching your journey to excellence.

"I am incredibly proud to be the Principal of Canons High School and I am delighted to welcome you to our school.
We are a diverse and inclusive comprehensive school that promotes high standards of excellence in all areas of school life. We are a community school where positive relationships are fundamental in enabling our young people to achieve their very best.
We have clear behaviour expectations which are fostered and supported with a comprehensive personal development programme which equips our students with the skills and opportunities needed to be successful members of society.
All students study a broad and innovative curriculum where we embrace new learning technologies to prepare students for future education and employment. We have a highly qualified and passionate staff who care deeply about the wellbeing of our young people.
Canons High School has a deep and rich history. It was formerly known as Downer Grammar School and was the first Grammar school to be built in Harrow after World War 2. It was named after Thomas Downer, a magistrate from Harrow who died in 1502. It became Canons High School in 1974 and recently celebrated its 50th anniversary. Canons was the name of one of the original four houses of the Grammar school and named after the local former country estate.
In September 2008 Canons High School established a Sixth Form and opened its new Sixth Form Centre in September 2009. It now has over 300 students studying advanced level subjects at Post 16.
The school officially gained Academy status in 2011 and in 2023 received its most recent Ofsted inspection achieving Good in all areas. It stated that ‘Leaders aspire to provide all pupils with a broad education within an inclusive environment. Pupils enjoy being part of a diverse school community, where they all feel valued." In 2024, we were awarded the Excellence in Personal Development Award and more recently achieved the Gold Award from the Teacher Development Trust for our outstanding CPD provision for staff.
We believe in Excellence for all:
Excellent behaviour & attitudes
Excellent teaching & learning
Excellent opportunities & experiences
Excellent outcomes & progress
Excellent communication
Excellent environment for learning
I hope this website gives you an insight into what makes this school special and encourages you to learn more about our community and its fantastic students."
Mr David Bullock - Principal

Welcome to Sixth Form
Miss Smith - Director of Sixth Form
Canons Sixth Form is much more that just a collection of classrooms, a common room and study spaces. It is a Community, with a culture and ethos that embodies and enables 'Excellence for all'.
We focus on bridging the gap between the curriculum and pastoral care to ensure students have both the academic, critical thinking and interpersonal skills to be self regulated both inside and outside of the classroom. Throughout their time in the Sixth Form, the Key Stage 5 pastoral team and coaches get to know students and offer high quality, on going academic intervention and personal development through our pastoral programme. The result of all of this is that our students have every chance possible to leave us and go on to enjoy great success in higher education and employment.

Languages Faculty
Head of Faculty: John Fenn
The Languages department at Canons supports students to become confident communicators who are prepared for life as global citizens. Throughout their career as students of French, Italian or Spanish, the aim of our language teaching is to increase student’s linguistic confidence, promote independence and raise intrinsic motivation. On arriving at Canons High School, all year 7 students have an opportunity to try our three timetabled languages during our Languages Carousel. They then opt for the language they would prefer to continue with for the rest of years 7, 8 & 9, and potentially into GCSE and beyond.
Learning a language is not just about becoming proficient in the skills of listening, speaking, reading, writing and translation. It is about developing an appreciation and understanding of the countries and communities who speak the language. To that end, our courses aim to engage students in learning about the cultures connected to the language they are studying, whether that be through developing their understanding of the food and drink, music, sport, customs and festivals, geography or literature related to communities who speak that language.
We value inclusivity highly and aim to actively support and celebrate diversity and multilingualism within our school community. In addition to our three taught languages, we offer students who are literate in their home language the opportunity to take a qualification in it. We regularly enter students for examinations in Arabic, Chinese, German, Gujarati, Persian, Polish, Portuguese, Turkish and Urdu, but actively seek to support students in other languages where a qualification is available.

Creative Performance and Media Arts Faculty
Head of Faculty: Leah Macnamara
The Creative, Performance and Media Arts Faculty is comprised of Art, Drama, Media Studies, Photography and Music, all of which are popular choices for students for both GCSE and A level and are studied by all students at KS3. As part of the Creative Arts community students get the opportunity to explore a range of different creative subjects in a unique learning environment. Our main priority is to ensure that our students receive a high standard of teaching and learning, and this is reflective in our excellent results and the many students who go on to pursue careers in the Creative Industries.
A large focus of The Creative Arts Faculty is the extra-curricular programme that is led by our experienced team. Each year we run a school musical which is open to all of our Creative Arts
Our students thrive in performing in a professional standard production. Previous shows have included Little Shop of Horrors, Bugsy Malone and Fame.
Additionally, our students have access to Media, Music, Drama, Art and Photography clubs and competitions and many students take part in Harrow Music Services instrumental lessons. We also regularly visit the theatre and various galleries in the West End. Former Creative Arts students have gone on to have leading roles in West End productions, work in the media, study music at Cambridge and work in a variety of exciting jobs in the creative industries.

Mathematics Faculty
Head of Faculty: Harsh Shah
At Canons High School, we believe that Mathematics is both relevant and important for success in life. We encourage all our students to learn maths without limits and in doing so, behave like ambitious mathematicians.
Mathematics is a hierarchical subject steeped in academic rigour. We want our students to foster a love for the beauty of the subject that goes beyond superficial enjoyment. This can only be experienced when they work and think hard about new knowledge, which is on the cusp of what they do know and can do independently.
Ascertaining students' existing knowledge, filling prior knowledge gaps, and then connecting new learning is at the heart of what we aim to do in the CHS Mathematics Faculty. Our curriculum maps and assessment models are based on this inclusive ethos to ensure that progress happens, and is visible to students over time.

pageCache.pageTitle: Canons High School - Religious Education Faculty
pageCache.text:
Religious Education Faculty
Head of Faculty: Adam Litchfield
Religion is about exploring and understanding the world around us. Religion has always been with us. Throughout history, it has expressed the deepest questions human beings can ask, and it has taken a central place in the lives of virtually all civilizations and cultures. RE allows students to explore ultimate questions such as: Why are we here? Where does evil come from? What happens when we die?
In modern times religion may not be so obviously prominent in the lives of many, yet the claims of religion continue to persist even as scientific and non-religious perspectives have become ever advancing. We still find religion everywhere, on television, in film, in popular music, in our community. We discover religion at the centre of global issues and cultural conflict. We see religion in the lives of the people we know and love, and in ourselves, as we grow and discover the person that we are.
Overall, religion is a powerful and persistent part of humanity. It provokes intense debate and critical questions, after all each and every one of us wants to know more about the world around us and ultimately what our the meaning and purpose is amongst it all.
Through the study of RE you will be able to make direct observations about the world around you, you will learn how to think critically and form philosophical questions, you will gain a cross-cultural understanding of the beliefs and practices that are ever increasing in modern society.
Students who have studied A-Level Religious Education have gone on to careers in politics, the civil service, law, the police, medicine, education and many more.
